newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke disagrees with BOE over rate rise need.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke disagrees with BOE over rate rise need.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday he disagreed with the Bank of England that UK interest rates needed to rise.
"I am disagreeing with him (Governor of the Bank of England Eddie George) over one quarter of one percent on interest rates," he told BBC radio in an interview.
He said the Bank was arguing the economy was recovering so strongly that the time has come to start raising rates.

"I disagree. I think we are recovering extremely strongly, but things have been going steadily since Christmas and show no sign of speeding up. I think it is not yet at the stage where I have to put the brakes on," Clarke added.
He said the authorities were looking at what inflation should be two years or so ahead.
"The Bank said it thinks it will be about 3.0 percent which is too high. I think it is most likely to be about 2.5 percent or less," Clarke said.
"I think, particularly given the strength of sterling, we are on course to meet 2.5 percent," Clarke said.
He said economic growth was steady. "What we have steady growth. I think consumers are very cautious."
Clarke said public borrowing had been halved and was still coming down.
"We have got one of the lowest debt to GDP ratios in Europe. So far as annual borrowing is concerned, I have halved it in my time as Chancellor and it's still going down."
